name: Rising Smoke Plume
question: How does buoyancy turn a smooth column into a turbulent plume?
blurb: A source of buoyant, dyed fluid at the floor. The column rises, shears against the still air, rolls up into vortices and entrains its surroundings.
physics:
Heat a parcel of fluid and it expands, becomes less dense than its surroundings, and is pushed upward by buoyancy — Archimedes' principle in a moving fluid. A continuous hot source therefore drives a rising column. As the column rises it drags still fluid along its edges; the velocity difference creates shear, the shear rolls up into vortices, and those vortices entrain surrounding fluid and tangle into the turbulent, billowing structure we call a plume.

Mathematically this is the incompressible Navier–Stokes system: conservation of momentum for a fluid whose density is treated as constant except in the buoyancy term (the Boussinesq approximation). The flow must also satisfy incompressibility, ∇·u = 0 — locally as much fluid leaves a point as enters it. That single constraint is what makes incompressible flow hard: the pressure is not a thermodynamic variable here but a Lagrange multiplier that instantly adjusts everywhere to keep the velocity divergence-free.

The same equations and solver govern visual-effects smoke, the dispersion of pollutants and volcanic plumes, and ventilation and fire modelling in buildings.
terms:
• u — the fluid velocity field
• ∂t u + (u·∇)u — acceleration of a fluid parcel (local + convective)
• −∇p — the pressure-gradient force that enforces incompressibility
• ν∇²u — viscous diffusion of momentum (friction)
• f_b — the buoyancy body force, proportional to temperature/dye
• ∇·u = 0 — incompressibility: the velocity field has no sources or sinks
numerics: A projection ('stable fluids') method: unconditionally-stable semi-Lagrangian advection, a red-black Gauss–Seidel SOR solve of the pressure-Poisson equation to enforce ∇·u = 0, a Boussinesq buoyancy force proportional to the transported temperature/dye, and vorticity confinement that re-injects the fine swirls numerical diffusion erodes.
ic: Quiescent ambient fluid with no dye; the source switches on at t = 0.
bc: No-penetration (free-slip) floor carrying a hot, dyed source patch; free-slip side walls; open (zero-gradient) top so the plume can leave the domain.
validation: Qualitative demonstration: the projection method keeps the flow divergence-free to the solver tolerance; vorticity confinement is a visual modelling term, not a physical property.

params.name: buoyancy
params.label: Buoyancy coefficient
params.help: Buoyancy coefficient: force per unit of the transported scalar (dye/temperature). Higher → a faster, more vigorous plume.

params.name: confinement
params.label: Vorticity confinement
params.help: Vorticity confinement — re-injects small-scale swirl lost to numerical diffusion (a modelling knob, not a physical property). 0 = none.

params.name: viscosity
params.label: Viscosity
params.help: Kinematic viscosity ν — how 'thick' the fluid is. Lower → finer, more chaotic structures; higher → smoother, damped flow.

params.name: flicker
params.label: Source flicker
params.help: Wobble & pulse the source (a prescribed modulation of the inflow, not a physical instability). 0 = a steady column; 1 = a lively, flame-like pulse.

params.name: source
params.label: Source width
params.help: Width of the hot source at the floor.

params.name: resolution
params.label: Resolution
params.help: Grid resolution. It changes the grid, and with it whatever a scene ties to the grid: the elapsed convective time in the wind tunnel, the Rayleigh number in the convection scenes, the grain size in the rock, the extent of the blast box. The derived readouts say what moved for this experiment; runs at different resolutions are comparable only where they say so.

params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).
